clue.text: Short tree-lined road in Leeds perhaps shows pothole?

indicators.note: in places the shortened road inside the place that Leeds exemplifies

blocks.note: Leeds is an example of a city
an avenue is a tree-lined road; short for it is the abbreviation AV

explanation.surface: A complaint that a leafy avenue in Leeds has a hole in its road surface.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a pothole is only one kind of hollow, and Leeds is just one example of a city.
explanation.definitionFit: A pothole is a hollow dug into a road or rock, which is an example of a hollow space.

clue.text: Charlie's a big awkward person, one who loves nightlife

blocks.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a lubber is a big clumsy oaf

explanation.surface: A description of someone called Charlie: hulking and clumsy, and a night owl.
explanation.definitionFit: A clubber is someone who regularly goes to nightclubs, so a fan of going out at night.

clue.text: As mentioned earlier corrupt adviser's happy to intervene

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or perverted, so the letters are put out of order
to intervene is to come between, so this word is placed inside the jumble

blocks.note: taken as written
up means cheerful, in high spirits

explanation.surface: As noted before, a bent consultant is glad to step in.
explanation.walkthrough: Vide supra is Latin, used in writing to send the reader back to an earlier passage.
explanation.definitionFit: Vide supra is Latin for see above, a note referring the reader to something stated earlier in the text.

clue.text: One's supporting unbelievable composer

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed below, so this part comes second

blocks.note: a tall story is one hard to believe
one is I, and the 's is IS

explanation.surface: Someone backing a composer whose work is incredible.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Tallis was an English Tudor composer of church music.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Tallis was a sixteenth-century English writer of sacred choral music.

clue.text: Template used for a decoration

indicators.note: something used has been worked over and reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A craft instruction: a stencil was used to make an ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: A palmette is an ornamental motif shaped like a fan of palm leaves, used in architecture and art.

clue.text: Book a singer-songwriter called Tori

blocks.note: first meaning: a book of the Old Testament
second meaning: the surname of the American musician Tori

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests booking a musician for a gig; 'Book' is really a noun naming a book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is a prophet's book in the Old Testament and the surname of the American musician Tori Amos.

clue.text: Sociologist's network swamped by rising River Test

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read upwards, so the order is turned round
swamped by means engulfed, so the network sits inside the other letters

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for river
an exam is a test
a web is a network

explanation.surface: A flood report: a net is submerged as the Test, a Hampshire river, rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River Test' looks like the Hampshire river's name, but it splits into R and EXAM. Max Weber was a German founder of sociology.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Weber was a German thinker regarded as one of the founders of modern sociology.

clue.text: Belgian city in which you won't find an insignificant person

indicators.note: you won't find it means those letters are missing from the city name

blocks.note: Antwerp is a port city in Belgium
taken as written

explanation.surface: A slight on a Belgian city where nobody of no account lives.
explanation.walkthrough: ANTWERP without AN leaves TWERP; 'an' looks like a mere article but is the letters removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A twerp is a silly or contemptible person, a nobody of little worth.

clue.text: Lead character in Sophocles' Electra

blocks.note: surface reading: the protagonist of the Greek tragedy, Electra herself
setter's reading: the first letter of the title as Sophocles would have written it in Greek

explanation.walkthrough: Character means a letter, not a role: the title's first letter in the Greek alphabet is named here.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra begins with E, and in Sophocles' Greek that letter is epsilon, the fifth of the alphabet.

clue.text: Rebellious Republican overruled by Democrat more than is necessary

indicators.note: overruled means the Republican letter is set aside and the Democrat letter takes its place

blocks.note: unruly means disorderly and rebellious
R is the abbreviation for Republican
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: An American political story: a rebel Republican outvoted by a Democrat, beyond what was needed.
explanation.walkthrough: The R of UNRULY is swapped for D, giving UNDULY.
explanation.definitionFit: Unduly is an adverb meaning excessively, to a degree beyond what is warranted.

clue.text: Ninety tablets hidden in body parts - that's too much!

indicators.note: something hidden in a thing is tucked inside it, so these letters go within the body parts

blocks.note: toes are parts of the body
XC is ninety in Roman numerals
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet, so tablets are Es

explanation.surface: A drug-smuggling exposé: ninety pills stashed about someone's person, which is outrageous.
explanation.walkthrough: E is slang for an ecstasy pill. The definition is the exclamation itself, the comment someone makes on excess.
explanation.definitionFit: To excess means beyond reasonable limits, which is what someone exclaiming that's too much objects to.

clue.text: Appropriate appearance to become widely known

blocks.note: to appropriate something is to take it
an air is a manner or look, as in an air of confidence

explanation.surface: Advice on looking the part in order to become famous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' reads as the adjective meaning suitable, but it is the verb meaning to seize.
explanation.definitionFit: When news takes air it gets out and spreads, becoming public knowledge.

clue.text: Book review of Life in France includes street event on the South coast

indicators.note: a review looks back over something, so the French phrase is read in the backward direction
includes means the street abbreviation is held within the other letters

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for book
la vie is French for life
ST is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A literary review of a book about French life that mentions a street party in a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book review' looks like one idea, but it splits into B and a signal to read LA VIE backwards, with ST inside: BESTIVAL is a music festival on the Isle of Wight.
explanation.definitionFit: Bestival was a music festival held on the Isle of Wight, just off England's south coast.

clue.text: Co-author?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone who writes a book jointly with another writer
setter's reading: a friend you write letters to and who writes back, so you write together

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark warns that co-author is not meant in the publishing sense: two correspondents are both authors of their exchange of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen pal is a friend made through exchanging letters, so each is writing alongside the other.

clue.text: Pub changing hands at last: drama for Swiss lakeside town

indicators.note: changing hands swaps left for right, and at last says it is the final letter that changes

blocks.note: a local is one's neighbourhood pub
No or Noh is classical Japanese masked drama

explanation.surface: A pub changes owners and becomes a theatre in a Swiss resort.
explanation.walkthrough: The final L (left) of LOCAL becomes R (right). Locarno sits on Lake Maggiore.
explanation.definitionFit: Locarno is a resort in Ticino, southern Switzerland, on the shore of Lake Maggiore.

clue.text: Criticised loudly being spellbound

indicators.note: loudly means the word is spoken out and judged by its sound

blocks.note: rapped means criticised sharply, as in rapped over the knuckles

explanation.surface: Someone was told off noisily while they sat entranced.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapt describes someone completely absorbed and enthralled, as if held by a spell.

clue.text: Early warning: terribly bad news shortly coming around

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly mangled, so these letters are jumbled
shortly means the phrase is cut short, losing its final letter
coming around means the jumbled letters wrap themselves about the golfer's call

blocks.note: taken as written
fore is the warning shout on a golf course

explanation.surface: An early warning that awful news is about to arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: BAD NEWS loses its S, is rearranged, and wraps around FORE, the golfer's shout to people in the ball's path.
explanation.definitionFit: Before dawn means in the small hours ahead of sunrise, so very early in the day.

clue.text: Old Greek prince maybe let loose

indicators.note: let loose means set free and scattered, so these letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: a prince is an example of an aristocrat, informally an aristo
taken as written

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek royal set free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let loose' reads as one phrase, but 'let' is the fodder and 'loose' alone is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was a philosopher of ancient Greece, a pupil of Plato.

clue.text: A person involved in blame game produces fertiliser

indicators.note: a game leg is a lame or damaged one, so the word is knocked out of shape
involved in means caught up inside, so the person goes within the jumble

blocks.note: one means a person, as in one who knows
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone caught up in a round of finger-pointing ends up producing manure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blame game' reads as a set phrase, but 'game' is the signal, in its sense of lame.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonemeal is ground animal bones, spread on soil as a slow-release fertiliser.

clue.text: Italian national strangely welcomes extremists from Piemonte but not together

indicators.note: strangely means the word is put into an odd, unfamiliar order
extremists are those at the far ends, so only the outermost letters of the region are kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the first and last letters of Piemonte

explanation.surface: An Italian citizen hosts hardliners from Piedmont, though they keep apart.
explanation.walkthrough: NATIONAL takes in P and E, and 'but not together' notes that the two added letters end up apart in the rearranged word.
explanation.definitionFit: Neapolitan means from Naples, so a Neapolitan is a particular kind of Italian person.

clue.text: Want some time off? Mr Davey goes away next

indicators.note: goes away means the politician's first name leaves the phrase

blocks.note: someone wanting time off would say they need a rest
Ed Davey is the Liberal Democrat leader

explanation.surface: A question to a weary politician, followed by his departure.
explanation.walkthrough: NEED A REST loses ED, the first name of the Liberal Democrat leader Ed Davey.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearest and next both mean the one closest in position, as in next door or the nearest house.

clue.text: Friendly type

blocks.note: first meaning: warm, considerate and generous
second meaning: a sort or category

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a friendly sort of person, but the two words are separate meanings, an adjective and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as an adjective for gentle, warm behaviour and as a noun meaning a sort or class.

clue.text: Gifted revolutionary, not dead

indicators.note: revolutionary means overturning the established order, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A talented rebel who has survived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gifted' reads as talented, but here it is the verb meaning given away.
explanation.definitionFit: Gifted as a past participle means given as a present, which is what donated means.

clue.text: Straight adult aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard means on board, so this letter is inside the vessel

blocks.note: a liner is a large passenger ship
A is the abbreviation for adult, as in film ratings

explanation.surface: An honest grown-up passenger on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Linear means arranged in or along a straight line.

clue.text: French detective ignoring head of MI6, it's a feather in his cap

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving something out, here the leading letter named
head of points to the first letter of the spy agency's name as the one dropped

blocks.note: Maigret is Simenon's French police detective
first letter of MI6

explanation.surface: A French sleuth outsmarting British intelligence, which is a feather in his cap.
explanation.walkthrough: MAIGRET loses its M. The idiom 'a feather in his cap' is read literally: an aigret is a plume worn on a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: An aigret or aigrette is a tuft of egret plumes worn as an ornament on a hat or headdress.

clue.text: Mathematician rejects answer but accepts 2.718 as estimate

indicators.note: rejects means throws out, so a letter is removed from the name
accepts means takes in, so the constant goes inside what remains

blocks.note: Carl Friedrich Gauss was a German mathematician
A is the abbreviation for answer
2.718 is the approximate value of the mathematical constant e

explanation.surface: A mathematician turns down an exact result and settles for an approximation.
explanation.walkthrough: The removed letter and the added one sit in different places, so this is not a straight swap; e, about 2.718, is the base of natural logarithms.
explanation.definitionFit: A guess is a rough judgement made without full information, which is an estimate.

clue.text: Demand family member to break into end of conversation

indicators.note: to break a word is to split it open, so the relative goes into the middle of the following word
end of means only the final letter of the talk word is used

blocks.note: taken as written
sis is short for sister
the last letter of conversation

explanation.surface: A sister insists on barging into a chat just as it is ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' looks like the container signal, but it is the word that gets broken open, and 'to' merely joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist on something is to demand it firmly and refuse to accept otherwise.

clue.text: "Females only" sign

blocks.note: if only females are present, there are zero, O, of the other sex
the other sex, counted as nil

explanation.surface: A notice on a door reserving a space for women.
explanation.walkthrough: Females only means no men, read as O MEN: zero men.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a portent, an event taken as a sign of what is to come.

clue.text: Maybe see twinkles, giving quick looks

blocks.note: to eye something is one way to see it
beams are rays or gleams of light, like twinkles

explanation.surface: Seeing sparkling lights as someone glances about.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyebeam is an old poetic word for a glance, imagined as a ray of light from the eye.

clue.text: Piece of music arranged in record time? The opposite

indicators.note: in says one part sits inside another
the opposite tells the solver to swap which part contains which

blocks.note: set means arranged, as a table is set
an EP is an extended-play record
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A tune arranged at speed, with a teasing instruction tacked on.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the clue puts the arranged word inside the record and time; 'The opposite' tells you to nest them the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: A septet is a composition written for seven voices or instruments.

clue.text: Seconds away from ex-PM, not telling the truth, having a fight

indicators.note: seconds away means the second letter of each following word is removed

blocks.note: Liz Truss was briefly UK prime minister in 2022
lying is not telling the truth

explanation.surface: A former prime minister caught out lying and squabbling, with a boxing-ring hint of seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seconds away' is the boxing call to start a round, which fits the fight; here it means each word loses its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tussling means grappling or scuffling with someone, so it is engaging in a struggle.

clue.text: For Macron nothing separates France from Germany, an ally

indicators.note: separates means it stands between the two country letters, holding them apart

blocks.note: F is the international vehicle code for France
rien is French for nothing, the word Macron would use
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: A diplomatic line: in the French president's view nothing comes between France and Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: A friend is someone on your side, which is what an ally is between nations.
